phase_0.boundary_condition: The spindle surface H(a,b) with R<r, enclosing the trapped factors within the toroidal geometry

⊢.justification: The uninitialized state before the semiprime N is loaded into the spindle coordinate system

⊣.justification: The closed toroidal surface that contains the entire factorization process

≻.justification: The directed transformation of factors along the spindle axis toward the throat

≺.justification: The descent transformation that reverses the winding direction to test factor stability

⋈.justification: The sequential chaining of prime factors p and q to form the semiprime N

⊙.justification: The identity mapping where the spindle recognizes the trapped factors as a stable pair

∈.justification: The splitting of the semiprime N into its two prime factors p and q

∋.justification: The rejoining of the separated factors p and q to verify their product N

⊤.justification: The constructive proof that p and q are indeed prime factors of N

⊥.justification: The constructive refutation that a candidate factor is not prime or does not divide N

⊞.justification: The state where both the trapped and released factors are held simultaneously in the spindle

⊡.justification: The permanent record of the trapped factors p and q in the spindle memory

phase_3.void_description: The empty spindle state before any factors are loaded
phase_3.true_description: The state where the factors p and q are successfully trapped and verified
phase_3.false_description: The state where the factors are not trapped or verification fails
phase_3.both_description: The state where the factors are both trapped and released simultaneously

steps.domain_action: Initialize the void state before loading the semiprime N
Wind the semiprime N forward along the spindle axis
Split the semiprime N into its two prime factors p and q
Affirm that p is a prime factor of N
Refute that p is not a prime factor of N
Rejoin the factors p and q to verify their product N
Recognize the trapped factors as a stable pair
Reverse the winding direction to test factor stability
Affirm that the factors remain trapped after reversal
Refute that the factors are released after reversal
Rejoin the factors to verify their stability
Record the trapped factors p and q in the spindle memory
Close the spindle boundary to contain the trapped factors

⊢=𐑨: Spindle mechanics implies a physical, extended arrangement where factors are trapped in a spatial structure rather than acting on a single point or through a purely temporal cycle.
⊞=𐑙: A semiprime consists of exactly two prime factors, and trapping them via spindle mechanics implies an equal, symmetric pairing of these components.
⊡=𐑴: Spindle mechanics implies a topological constraint where the factors are trapped in a way that prevents continuous deformation without crossing a discrete topological boundary.
⊙=𐑢: The description depicts a stable trapping mechanism where factors are contained rather than poised at a threshold of instability or undergoing scale-free fluctuations.
⊥=𐑒: Spindle mechanics implies a helical winding around a single axis that defines the chirality, but the trapping mechanism suggests a relatively simple, reversible orientation rather than a complex topological lock.

⋈=𐑐: The mechanical nature of spindle trapping, combined with the structural integrity implied by the other assigned primitives, suggests a geometry-enforcing mechanism that ensures the factors are captured with high reliability.
⊤=𐑧: The description of "trapping" factors via mechanical winding implies a high kinetic barrier where the system is effectively frozen and requires significant external driving to release or rearrange.
∈=𐑚: The spindle mechanics act on a specific structural motif (the semiprime pair) within the broader system, implying a mesoscale range of influence rather than a purely local event or a system-wide global propagation.
∋=𐑠: The spindle mechanics imply an ordered winding process where factors are engaged sequentially to form the trapped structure, rather than requiring simultaneous presence or a broad cooperative assembly.
